what_happened.line: Water commissioners asked the superintendent to check how Town Hall handles COVID exposure and pay and return with a temporary policy at the next meeting.
A man considering a run for the open commissioner seat was told to pull nomination papers and file them at the town clerk's office by the Monday deadline.
The superintendent reported that tank cleaning and inspection were done together at a negotiated price, and that the Chase Road tank is due to be painted.
The superintendent described a cellular-lease fee set aside for tank maintenance, and an estimated cost for painting the Chase Road tank, with lead paint adding expense.
The board reviewed warrants and prior minutes, then heard a report on recent main breaks and paving. No formal votes are recorded in the minutes.

why_it_matters: Tank painting is paid in part from cellular equipment lease fees set aside for maintenance, so it bears on how much of that work water rates must cover.
The open commissioner seat is filled by a vote residents will be asked to take, and the filing deadline decides who can be on the ballot.
A temporary COVID exposure and pay policy would set whether exposed water staff are paid while quarantined, which touches how reliably the service is staffed.
